subject: SLO measurement and metrics onboarding — procurement questionnaire
messages:
From: Helen Park <procurement@globex.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement questionnaire — SLO measurement and monitoring

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement has a short set of clarifying questions we need answered before we sign the MSA. Please see the three items below — if you can confirm by end of day Monday it will keep us on track for our internal approval.

1) How do you measure uptime and request latency for hosted customers? Is this measured at the edge (ingress) or at the backend worker?
2) How are SLOs instrumented and what alerting thresholds do you use (examples for 99.9% uptime and p95 latency)?
3) Can customers access raw metrics or dashboards for their account (read-only)? If so, what's the onboarding process and retention window?

We'd also appreciate any supporting artifacts (SLO definition, measurement appendix, sample dashboard link).

Best,
Helen Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Globex Corp

P.S. If there are any anticipated exceptions (e.g., onboarding warmup) we need the documented exception handling process so our legal team can review.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <procurement@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — SLO measurement and monitoring

Hi Helen —

Thanks for the questions and great conversation. Below are concise answers; I attached a filled-out questionnaire (procurement_questionnaire_answers.pdf) and a short measurement workbook (redwood_slo_measurement_v1.xlsx). Happy to hop on a quick call if anything needs more detail.

1) Measurement point: We compute uptime and latency from both ingress edge probes (control-plane synthetic probes per region) and server-side worker telemetry. The primary SLO is derived from edge-observed successful responses to customer tokens (this aligns with customer-perceived availability). Backend metrics are used for root-cause and alerting, but the SLA assertion is edge-observed.

2) Instrumentation & alerting: SLOs are computed from request logs (per-customer request tagging) aggregated on a 5-minute sliding window. Typical thresholds we operate with:
  - 99.9% availability (measured monthly) using HTTP 2xx as success. Alerting: page at sustained 5-minute error budget burn > 25%.
  - Latency: p95 and p99 measured at the edge. Example: p95 target 120ms for standard models; p99 target 450ms. Alerting on p95 drift: sustained 10% above target for 15 minutes triggers a P1 alert.

3) Customer access: We provide a read-only dashboard that exposes the SLO time series (availability, p95, p99), error budget burn rate, and per-region breakdown. Onboarding: we enable read-only role for an account admin after a signed DPA/MSA and a short access request. Retention: metrics retained at full resolution for 90 days; aggregated at hourly for 12 months.

Exceptions/process: We document onboarding warming exceptions in our runbook. Temporary exceptions (e.g., initial traffic warmup as you onboard large model weights) require a written request from the customer and approval from our support ops lead. When approved, the exception window and compensating monitoring (increased synthetic probes) are recorded and the effective SLO period is adjusted for billing and compliance.

I copied Marissa (Product) and Hiro (SRE) to confirm the retention and to add any technical notes.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: procurement_questionnaire_answers.pdf, redwood_slo_measurement_v1.xlsx

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — SLO measurement and monitoring

Kimberly — quick nit: do we want to confirm the retention policy for traces/logs vs metrics? Procurement sometimes asks for 1 year of raw traces which we don't keep. Suggest we explicitly call out: metrics full-res 90d, aggregated 12mo; raw request traces (headers/payload hashes) 30d unless an extended retention add-on is purchased.

Also, should we offer a standard dashboard share (read-only) vs. a BI export?

-on Marissa

Date: Sat, 04 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — SLO measurement and monitoring

Marissa/Hiro —

Thanks — agreed. I'm updating the questionnaire answers to be explicit about traces/logs. Hiro: can you confirm the default raw-trace retention and whether we have an add-on for 12mo? If so, mention the cost/ops lead in the doc.

Also, for exception handling language I'll add a short runbook excerpt (attached: runbook-slo-exceptions.md). Key points:
  - Exception request must be submitted 48 hours in advance for planned onboarding (for large model imports).
  - Emergency exceptions for hardware or region failovers require post-hoc exception logging; we do not pre-approve emergency exceptions except in rare cases and those will be subject to review.
  - Any approved exception will specify whether the measurement window is excluded for billing SLO purposes and will list compensating probes.

I'm going to send the finalized package to procurement after we confirm the trace retention line.

-Kim
